query: Map the data flow through a machine learning pipeline from raw data ingestion to model deployment as a diagram.
narrative:
Here is a general **data‑flow diagram** for an end‑to‑end machine learning pipeline, written in **Mermaid** so you can render it directly in tools that support it.[1][3][6][7][8]

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    %% ========= LAYERS =========
    subgraph S0["Data Sources"]
        s1["Operational DBs / Data Warehouse"]
        s2["Logs & Events"]
        s3["Files (CSV, Parquet, JSON)"]
        s4["External APIs / 3rd‑party data"]
        s5["User‑generated data"]
    end

    subgraph S1["Ingestion & Storage"]
        i1["Batch ingestion (ETL/ELT jobs)"]
        i2["Streaming ingestion (Kafka, Kinesis, etc.)"]
        i3["Raw data store / Data lake\n(object storage, lakehouse)"]
    end

    subgraph S2["Data Processing & Feature Engineering"]
        c1["Data cleaning & validation\n(schema checks, dedup, outlier handling)"]
        c2["Transformation\n(type casting, joins, aggregations)"]
        c3["Feature engineering\n(domain features, embeddings, encodings)"]
        c4["Feature store\n(online & offline views)"]
    end

    subgraph S3["Model Development & Training"]
        e1["Train/validation/test split\n(+ cross‑validation)"]
        e2["Model training\n(algorithms, hyperparameter search)"]
        e3["Model evaluation\n(metrics, bias/fairness checks)"]
        e4["Model registry\n(versioned models & metadata)"]
    end

    subgraph S4["Deployment & Serving"]
        d1["Deployment pipeline (CI/CD for ML)\n(build, test, promote)"]
        d2["Online inference service\n(REST/gRPC, low latency)"]
        d3["Batch scoring jobs\n(predictions written to tables/files)"]
    end

    subgraph S5["Monitoring, Feedback & Retraining"]
        m1["Monitoring\n(latency, errors, resource usage)"]
        m2["Data & prediction drift detection"]
        m3["Business KPI tracking"]
        m4["Feedback loop & labeling\n(ground truth collection)"]
        m5["Trigger retraining\n(on schedule or drift/quality events)"]
    end

    %% ========= DATA FLOW =========
    %% Sources -> Ingestion
    s1 --> i1
    s2 --> i2
    s3 --> i1
    s4 --> i1
    s5 --> i2

    %% Ingestion -> Raw store
    i1 --> i3
    i2 --> i3

    %% Raw store -> Processing & Features
    i3 --> c1
    c1 --> c2
    c2 --> c3
    c3 --> c4

    %% Features -> Training
    c4 --> e1
    e1 --> e2
    e2 --> e3
    e3 --> e4

    %% Registry -> Deployment
    e4 --> d1
    d1 --> d2
    d1 --> d3

    %% Inference uses features / raw data
    c4 --> d2
    i3 --> d3

    %% Serving -> Monitoring & Feedback
    d2 --> m1
    d2 --> m2
    d2 --> m3
    d3 --> m2
    d3 --> m3

    %% Feedback -> Retraining loop
    m2 --> m4
    m3 --> m4
    m4 --> m5
    m5 --> e1
```

---

**How to use this:**

- You can paste this code into any Mermaid‑compatible editor or documentation system to visualize the flow as a diagram.[1]  
- To simplify for teaching or slides, you can:
  - Collapse S1–S2 into a single **“Data pipeline (ETL/ELT)”** block if you only want a high‑level view.[2][4]  
  - Collapse S3–S5 into **“MLOps pipeline (train → deploy → monitor → retrain)”**.[5][6]  

---

**Major claims and confidence**

- The stages included (ingestion → processing → feature store → training → registry → deployment → monitoring → retraining) reflect standard ML pipeline anatomy and MLOps practice.[3][5][6][7][8]  
  - **Confidence: High**

- Using a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of tasks (e.g., for ETL/ELT and training orchestration) is a common implementation pattern.[2][5][6]  
  - **Confidence: High**
